sources: WooCommerce product reviews and orders exports (uploaded)
header.disclaimer: A summary of Google's and the FTC's published rules, not legal advice.

stop_first.practice: At pickup, mechanics ask customers who seem happy to leave us a Google review.
stop_first.problem: Review gating: only customers who seem happy are asked.
stop_first.rule: Google review policy: no selective soliciting of positive reviews.
stop_first.fix: Every workshop customer gets the same pickup text, whatever the mechanic thinks of the visit.

stop_first.practice: The receipt says: Leave us a 5-star review and get 10% off your next tune-up.
stop_first.problem: An incentive for a review, and the incentive is tied to a 5-star review.
stop_first.rule: Google review policy: no discounts or other incentives for posting any review. FTC rule (16 CFR Part 465, in force since 21 October 2024): no incentive conditioned on a review's sentiment.
stop_first.fix: Remove the line from the receipt today. Ask for an honest review, with no offer and no star count.

stop_first.practice: When we opened, both mechanics and the owner's brother posted Google reviews.
stop_first.problem: Reviews from staff and a relative.
stop_first.rule: Google review policy: no reviews with a conflict of interest, including employment. FTC rule: insider reviews need a clear disclosure of the connection.
stop_first.fix: Flag those reviews in the Business Profile for removal, or ask the writers to delete them, and keep staff to asking, never reviewing.

local_gap.rival_pace_basis: Change in each rival's count from 2026-07-29 to 2026-10-28 (2.99 months).
local_gap.customers_basis: Workshop jobs finished plus new bikes sold, averaged over the last 6 complete months: the customers who get the Google review ask. Online orders get the product review ask instead.

rating_outlook.note: If new reviews keep the last 6 months' average. Not a promise.

local_gap.finding: You get 3.3 reviews a month; passing Example Bicycle Co. by 2027-10-28 takes 10.2, 3.1 times today's pace. That means 4.2% of the 244 customers you serve each month leave a review, up from 1.4%. Today only some workshop customers are asked and new bike buyers are never asked.

google_minimums.rating: Product ratings (Shopping ads and free listings)
google_minimums.minimum: 50 reviews across all products, feed sent at least monthly
generally 100 eligible unique reviews in a rolling 24 months; 3.5 stars or higher to show on ads
google_minimums.note: Product reviews feed product ratings, not the store rating. The store has no store review source yet.

store_review_scenarios.label: Scenarios at response rates you choose, not benchmarks.

store_coverage.finding: 28 product reviews, 22 short of the 50 Google needs before any product shows stars, and nothing is asked after delivery today. 3 products sell at or above the median (190 units) with coverage under the store's 1.13 per 100 units; ask about these first.

email_new_bike.subject: How is the new bike riding?
email_new_bike.body: Hi {first name}, you've had your new bike for two weeks now. How is it riding? If you have a minute, an honest Google review helps other riders in Millbrook find a shop they can trust. [Write a review](https://search.google.com/local/writereview?placeid=EXAMPLE-PLACE-ID-EBW) Example Bike Works, 418 Mill Street, Millbrook. Unsubscribe.

email_online_order.subject: How is your order from Example Bike Works?
email_online_order.html:
Hi {{ first_name|default:'there' }},

Your {{ event.product_name }} arrived a few days ago. Now that you've had a chance to use it, would you tell other riders what you think?

Review your purchase

Good or bad, an honest review helps us and helps the next rider choose.

Example Bike Works, 418 Mill Street, Millbrook

{% unsubscribe 'Unsubscribe' %}

templates.qr_card: How did we do? Scan to leave an honest Google review. Example Bike Works
templates.receipt_line: How did we do? Leave an honest review: ebw.example/review
templates.removed: The receipt's 5-star and 10% off line is gone from every template.
templates.variables: first_name and event.product_name stand in for the variables your Klaviyo flow's trigger event provides; swap in yours.

rollout_and_tracking.weekly_review_target: 3 new reviews a week (10.2 a month)
rollout_and_tracking.who_sends: Pickup texts go out from the point-of-sale texting at pickup, emails from Klaviyo flows, and whoever hands back a bike gives the QR card.
week_1: Switch pickup texts to every customer.
Flag the staff and family reviews.
week_2: Save the online order email in Klaviyo (after your yes) and add it to a flow 6 days after fulfillment.
month_2: Enroll in Google Customer Reviews for the store.
Send product reviews to Merchant Center as a monthly feed once 50 are reached.
rollout_and_tracking.monthly: Rerun this skill: reviews gained vs the required pace, review rate vs customers served, average stars of new reviews, rivals' counts.
rollout_and_tracking.change_course_if: two months below 75% of 10.2, that is under 7.6 reviews a month

unknowns: The store's real response rate to a review request is unmeasured; the store rating timeline is a scenario.
Google's public review count may differ from the API list; check the profile if they disagree.
